conviction_note: The H1 beat against the company plan looks near-certain (Q1 OP was 60.9% of the H1 OP plan, against 46% at the same point in prior years, and in June the company said the Middle East effect was not in its plan). But that is computable from the July 短信, and the stock was already +6.3% at the 10:05 seal, ahead of an 11:30 release. The last beat of this size (Q1, OP +52.5%) came after a +4.5% run-in and was sold 4.6% the next day. So the findings sum to 0 and p_up sits just under 50. The one item that would move the stock is a full-year raise, and Konishi has not revised its full-year plan at a Q2 print in the last three years.

findings.finding: H1 will clear the company's H1 plan by a wide margin. Q1 OP of 3,257m is 60.9% of the 5,350m H1 OP plan, and Q1 ordinary profit is 62.2% of the H1 plan against 45.7% (FY25) and 46.4% (FY26) at the same quarter. Q2 needs only 2,093m OP against 2,747m and 2,486m in the last two Q2s.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-07-27, 15:30), OP +52.5%: stock +4.52% on the day before the release, then -4.59% the next session. Q2 FY26 (2025-10-28, 11:30): -3.40% / -3.44% over two sessions (Yahoo daily bars).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. kabutan publishes the 62.2% progress rate on its finance page (https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=4956), and the stock is +6.3% before the release. What may be left is the size: with zero analyst coverage nobody has published an H1 number, so the exact beat is unpriced while its direction is not.
findings.independence: Shares the Q1 短信 with the guidance finding below. The progress-rate history is a different source: https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=4956

findings.finding: The full-year plan leaves room to be raised at this print. The company told FISCO the Middle East effect (April pre-buying, 20%+ Bond price increases) was NOT in the FY27 plan. If H1 OP is about 5,800m, the 11,500m FY plan implies H2 OP of about 5,700m, below FY26's H2 of 5,842m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Konishi's revisions have come at Q3 or separately, not at Q2: full-year upward revision plus dividend increase 2024-01-26 (stock +2.8% / +3.9% around the 2024-01-29 Q3 print), dividend increases 2024-04-23 and 2025-02-18. kabutan's revision history shows no October full-year revision for FY24 to FY26.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market expected a raise, the stock would be re-rated on the raised number: PER 12.1 on the unrevised plan, which is roughly where the name has traded. No preview exists for a zero-coverage name. Sized small because the company's own record is to hold at Q2, and Middle East uncertainty is a ready reason to hold again.

findings.finding: The last beat was sold, and this release starts from a pre-release spike. The Q1 beat (OP +52.5%) was sold 4.59% the next session after a +4.52% run on release day, and the stock is +6.3% at the 10:05 seal today on above-normal volume with no news found, so the window's entry price already holds a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a question about what the +6.3% already holds, not a hidden fact. The baseline's lean (-0.35) carries the 20-day run-up but not today's intraday spike, which happened after most of the run-up window. If the move were fully understood the morning would have a cause on the wire, and I found none.

findings.finding: Q2 itself faces payback. The company's Q1 text attributes part of Q1 to April pre-buying on Middle East supply fears and describes shipment adjustments (出荷調整) to avoid stockouts, so Q2 standalone OP could print below last year's 2,486m even as H1 beats. Construction-segment profit deferred from Q1 into Q2+ partly offsets.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 (household Bond weak, net -1%, Nikkei 2025-11-20): -6.73% over two sessions.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the pre-buying is disclosed. What is not is whether the 7-9月 headline reads as a YoY decline, which kabutan-style headlines will print separately from the H1 beat.

outside_window.finding: Dividend policy is a 30% payout and FY EPS guidance is 131.21 yen against a 38 yen dividend (29%). A net-profit beat makes a year-end dividend increase plausible, but Konishi has announced its increases at Q3 or at the year-end (2024-01-26, 2024-04-23, 2025-02-18), not at Q2.

baseline_tension: The fundamentals point up (a near-certain H1 beat and an unplanned windfall), against a stock that has run +7.8% over 20 days, +6.3% of it this morning before the release, and that sold its last beat. The strongest positive the release could carry is a full-year raise (I looked: no pre-release revision, and no Q2 raise in the company's record) or a buyback (I looked: buybacks have come at Q1 and Feb). The weak margin long side (0.83) cushions the downside.
lessons_applied: Open question 4 (a five-day run-in sized as a negative, which rose 8.15% on its single case) made me shrink the reaction-history/run-in positioning finding from -1.2 to -0.9; I kept it negative because this name's own July beat was sold after a same-day run.
Rule 1 (a negative resting on a series anyone can compute is priced) moved the Q2 payback finding, which rests on the public Q1 短信 text, from -0.3 to -0.2, and p_up from 45 to 47.
Rule 2: two negatives against three positives; I wrote the strongest positive (a full-year raise or buyback) into baseline_tension and recorded that I looked for it. Nothing else moved.
